text:
marta: Hey team -- customer reported sudden throughput drop on /v1/generate around 2026-11-02 14:03 UTC, p95 jumped from 220ms to ~1.2s across a 10m window. They gave a few sample request IDs: r-0a1b2c3d r-0f5e6d7c.
sujay: Thanks Marta. Can we get a minimal repro from them and a curl pack? ask for: exact curl commands, concurrency profile, promptset (10-20 examples) and approximate token counts. Also need full list of request ids and timestamps.
customer-ops: Confirmed, we can run a short reproducible script. We'll collect 50 concurrent requests for 2 minutes starting 14:02:30 UTC. We'll attach ids.
sujay: Perfect. Share this recommended repro checklist with them:
- include X-Request-Id header on each request (or note the returned request id)
- capture a HAR if using browser UI or run curl with --trace-ascii to capture timing
- provide the exact payloads (promptset) and max_tokens used
- indicate concurrency pattern (steady ramp, burst, etc.)
- include server region and API key (redact key)
- if possible, run a debug bundle collector script from their side and upload to the support share

marta: I pasted a short curl example for them:
```bash
# single request example (please replace $KEY and $REQID)
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
  -H "X-Request-Id: repro-req-001"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"Summarize: The quick brown fox","max_tokens":64}'
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
And a tiny concurrency loop: `for i in {1..40}; do curl ... -H "X-Request-Id: repro-$i" & done; wait`

sujay: Also ask them to run this to capture timing and response headers to disk: `curl -w "\nTIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\n" -o /dev/null -s -D headers_repro.txt ...`

ben: If they can't run HAR we can accept a list of request ids and we'll cross-reference with backend traces. But HAR + curl ids = fastest.

support-bot: FYI I've created a support artifact folder: s3://redwood-support/debug-uploads/1805123456/ waiting for upload link.

customer-ops: Uploaded a tarball: https://redwood-support.s3.amazonaws.com/debug-uploads/1805123456/customer123-repro.tar.gz includes:
- curl-pack.json (40 payloads)
- request_ids.txt (list of 120 ids covering the window)
- timing_traces/ (curl traces)

marta: Got it. Starting a targeted trace pull for those ids.
sujay: When you uploaded, did you include the concurrency driver you used? steady 40qps or burst?
customer-ops: We used steady concurrency: 40 parallel workers, each sending ~1 request every 3s for 2 minutes. Token counts varied 24-180.

sujay: Excellent. Two quick asks for a focused repro pack:
1) Can you re-run with a fixed small promptset of 10 prompts with similar token distribution and label each with repro-req- tag?
2) Include one run that's pure short prompts (~20 tokens) and one that's long (~150 tokens) so we can see tail behavior.

ben: I'm kicking off an internal replay against the serving logs now. If we see model kernel stall or batching anomalies I'll report back.

support-bot: Trace request r-0a1b2c3d found across gateway -> router -> serving node 12. Collected kvcache metrics snapshot attached to artifact.

marta: Noted. Also asking infra to check for colocation GC noise on node 12 during window.

customer-ops: Re-ran with 10-prompt set and uploaded results to the same bucket: customer123-repro-v2.tar.gz. Included a README with the exact run command and a shell snippet: `for i in $(seq 1 10); do curl -s -H "X-Request-Id: repro-v2-$i" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d "@payloads/p$i.json" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate & done; wait`

sujay: Great — I'll attach the run ids to the debug ticket and link to the repro pack for eng-runtime to reproduce locally.

ben: Initial replay shows 2x increase in serialization time inside our kernel selection path for requests with tokens >120. Filing a followup in eng-runtime.
marta: Thanks — follow up with the exact request ids where cost jumped (I want them in the ticket).

support-bot: Thread pinned to ticket #SUP-8743. :white_check_mark:

customer-ops: Thanks everyone. We'll stand by for eng updates and can run any additional runs you need. :raised_hands:
